decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
I chose Mongoose ODM (mongoose) with an Express REST surface.
alternatives: Use Mongoose ODM with schemas and transactions
reason: Prompt explicitly requested Mongoose; Mongoose provides schema enforcement, validation, and integration with transactions which suit a readable sample app.
evidence: Sample prompt: 'Using the DocumentDB skill, build a Node.js Mongoose core banking ledger'

decision: I chose Mongoose 7.6.0 (pin exact version in package.json).
reason: Mongoose 7.x is the recommended modern major line and is compatible with Node 24; pinning an exact 7.x release avoids unexpected upgrades for sample users.
evidence: Readiness report: 'Builder will pick a recent Mongoose compatible with Node 24 (e.g., Mongoose 7.x) and the MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol.'

decision: I chose to default to SCRAM credentials read from DOCUMENTDB_URI in environment variables, with README notes about Entra ID as optional.
alternatives: Implement Microsoft Entra ID OIDC auth by default
reason: Simpler for local development; cluster supports SCRAM and DOCUMENTDB_URI is available in environment per run environment notes.
evidence: Readiness guidance: 'Default to SCRAM credential auth via DOCUMENTDB_URI for the sample; optionally add an enable Entra ID code path'

decision: I chose to expose a small REST API (POST /transactions, GET /accounts/:id) plus an npm-run seed CLI script.
alternatives: Expose REST API endpoints and CLI seed script
reason: REST API demonstrates atomic posting and retrieval; seed script allows idempotent sample data loading; matches reviewer assumptions and is easy to run manually.
evidence: Assumptions from prompt review recommended REST API and seed script.

decision: I chose to create the unique index on transactions.transactionRef and a compound index {accountId:1, createdAt:-1}.
alternatives: Also add compound index on accountId + createdAt
reason: Unique index enforces idempotency; compound index supports recent-activity queries used by GET /accounts/:id.
evidence: Assumptions from prompt review: 'At minimum create a unique index on transactions.transactionRef. Also create an index on transactions.accountId and transactions.createdAt'

decision: I chose npm to install dependencies and run scripts.
reason: npm is available and standard; simpler for sample users and matches run environment.
evidence: Environment: Node.js and npm/npx available per readiness report.

decision: I chose to run the seed script against the live cluster to create sample data for verification.
alternatives: Do not run seed, only create code
Run seed script against live cluster to create sample data
reason: Seed data is required to demonstrate atomic transactions and to verify indexes and queries; run_policy allows non-Azure resource commands like node scripts to run against the cluster.
evidence: Run environment: 'This sample is being built on a developer machine where an Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable... DOCUMENTDB_URI in environment'

decision: I approved the build with readiness 'ready_with_gaps'
I chose Node.js with Express and Mongoose.
reason: Node.js with Mongoose is the recommended quickstart for Azure DocumentDB and matches the environment (Node 24 available). It makes MongoDB transactions and Mongoose models simple for readers.
evidence: Assumption: 'Builder will implement a single-agent, no-orchestration sample (a standalone Node.js app with local CLI and/or HTTP endpoints).'

reason: Mongoose 7.x is stable, widely used and compatible with modern Node; no Node-24-specific authoritative version was available so I selected 7.x and will pin an explicit version in package.json.
evidence: Readiness report: 'Builder will pick a recent Mongoose compatible with Node 24 (e.g., Mongoose 7.x)'

decision: I chose SCRAM credential authentication via DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable.
alternatives: SCRAM auth via connection string env var
Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) auth via DefaultAzureCredential
reason: SCRAM is simplest for sample and the environment provides DOCUMENTDB_URI; avoid complexity of Entra ID flows for this demo.
evidence: Readiness guidance: 'Default to SCRAM credential auth via DOCUMENTDB_URI for the sample; optionally add an enable Entra ID code path.'

decision: I chose to use the existing cluster and not provision any Azure resources.
alternatives: Use existing cluster and do not provision
reason: No infra changes are required and policy forbids provisioning; sample will run against provided cluster.
evidence: Run environment: 'a Azure DocumentDB cluster is already provisioned and reachable ... DOCUMENTDB_URI' and run policy forbids Azure resource changes.

decision: I chose REST API plus CLI scripts (seed and demo) in a single Node.js app.
reason: This gives both programmatic and interactive ways to exercise the sample while keeping the project small and easy to run.
evidence: Assumption: 'Builder will expose a small REST API: POST /transactions ... and a CLI script (npm run seed) to load sample data.'

decision: I chose to create both a unique index on transactions.transactionRef and a compound index on { accountId:1, createdAt:-1 }.
reason: Unique index enforces idempotency; compound index supports recent-activity queries per account efficiently.
evidence: Assumption: 'At minimum create a unique index on transactions.transactionRef. Also create an index on transactions.accountId and transactions.createdAt.'

decision: I chose to change mongoose dependency to "^7.0.0" after npm reported no matching 7.9.3 version.
reason: Using a caret range ^7.0.0 lets npm pick a valid 7.x release available in the registry and avoids our earlier incorrect pin; this is safer for installation in the ephemeral environment.
evidence: npm error: "No matching version found for mongoose@7.9.3."

decision: I chose two collections: accounts (snapshot of balance) and transactions (immutable ledger documents).
reason: This model cleanly separates immutable ledger entries from account balance snapshot, makes recent-activity queries efficient, and matches the prompt requirements for multi-document transactions.
evidence: Prompt: 'store every debit and credit as an immutable document in DocumentDB. Use multi-document transactions to atomically append the transaction and update the account balance snapshot.'
